title: A Google Calendar event claims an issue fixed that never actually closed
author: retrya
description: The Calendar-side twin of mention-claims-unfixed-issue (the X-mention leg), slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue (the Slack-channel leg), linear-comment-claims-unfixed-issue (the Linear-comment leg), and email-claims-unfixed-issue (the Gmail leg) -- and the first recipe under RECIPES/ to read a Google Calendar event's own title/description as a claim-bearing text surface. Grepped every one of the 101 existing recipes' own recipe.json toolkit field before writing this one: google_calendar appears in exactly one place, milestone-deadline-no-calendar-event's own github+google_calendar -- and that recipe only ever matches an event's title against a milestone's due date by keyword-overlap and time window, never parsing an event's own free text for a closing-keyword promise. Extracts every real GitHub closing-keyword claim (fixes/closes/resolves #N, both tenses, the shared seam_engine.closing_keywords grammar) from a calendar event's own title+description and cross-checks it against the live issue tracker's own state -- a meeting note or agenda line sitting on a connected calendar is exactly as durable and readable-later as a tweet, a mention, a Slack message, a Linear comment, or an email, and nothing on either platform ever compares it against the issue tracker's real state. Proposed per CONTRIBUTING.md's own 'New toolkits' section, the exact same way gmail_calendar.py, slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue, linear-comment-claims-unfixed-issue, and email-claims-unfixed-issue each proposed their own toolkit's first text-reading recipe before it had a live wired tool -- fixture-only, MOCK ONLY, never a live network call.
confidence_notes: Age-gated by hours since the event's own start time, holding email-claims-unfixed-issue's/mention-claims-unfixed-issue's/slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue's/linear-comment-claims-unfixed-issue's identical 0.85/0.5 bar exactly -- not an independently re-reasoned number just because the toolkit's text-reading door is new. A claim checked within 24 hours of the event's own start might still be a race (the real fix landing moments after the meeting) rather than a settled overclaim (0.5, below the 0.70 confidence bar, shown as a weighed-and-dropped coincidence, not hidden). At or past 24 hours with the named issue still open, it is unambiguous (flat 0.85). The check itself is objective, same reasoning as every claims-unfixed-issue sibling: the claimed issue's own live state field, verified against ListIssues, not a guess about which tracker the organizer meant. A named issue that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- a broken reference is a future calendar-side dangling-reference recipe's own seam, not this one's. A named issue that IS closed is excluded too -- the claim was simply true. An event with no closing-keyword claim phrase at all produces no candidate. No text in this recipe's own headline/detail strings ever names or grades the organizer -- CONTRIBUTING.md's 'No grading, ever' law, same as every recipe in this engine.
